rv.q: He follows the same route by exploring the African American experience, with a predominantly Black cast and references to Igbo culture, but without enough conviction to this central idea. There is a burst of ritual at the end, but a lack of purpose to the occasional Igbo-translated lines.

Death of a Salesman by Arthur Miller follows Willie Loman, an aging salesman who is struggling with his career, his mental health and his relationship with his family, especially his son Biff. Willie has always believed that being successful and well-liked is the key to a good life, and he has placed these expectations onto his sons.

Once again, Death to the Salesman returns to the stage- full of light, music and lively energy- and I think it’s safe to say, extremely far from dull. Like many of Miller’s works, Death of a Salesman is a classic American “problem play” and social critique.
